recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片鐵染色下多顆中晚期紅母細胞（核小而染色質粗）在核周分布一圈藍色鐵顆粒，另可見早期大細胞沒有鐵顆粒，左上角有細胞外鐵塊，符合多量環狀鐵粒母細胞。
features: Prussian blue-stained aspirate with red nuclear counterstain
Multiple intermediate to late erythroid precursors with coarse blue granules arranged around the nucleus (ring sideroblasts)
Ring sideroblasts are the predominant iron-containing cells in the field
Larger immature cells with fine chromatin and no siderotic granules
Small aggregate of extracellular stainable iron at the upper left
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear stained with Prussian blue shows multiple intermediate and late erythroid precursors with coarse blue siderotic granules distributed around the nucleus, many encircling at least one-third of the nuclear circumference, consistent with ring sideroblasts. Larger immature nucleated cells lack stainable iron, and a small extracellular iron fragment is present. Ring sideroblasts appear frequent in this field, but a formal count of at least 100 erythroid precursors is required for classification. Findings are consistent with numerous ring sideroblasts, supporting myelodysplastic neoplasm with ring sideroblasts in this context.

ddx.dx: Reactive sideroblastic change (alcohol, isoniazid, linezolid, copper deficiency, zinc excess)
ddx.vs: Morphology is identical, so exclusion depends on history, copper and zinc levels, and resolution after removal of the cause.

ddx.dx: AML with myelodysplasia-related changes or MDS with excess blasts with ring sideroblasts
ddx.vs: Ring sideroblasts occur in these too, so the blast percentage on the Wright-stained aspirate and CD34 on biopsy must be assessed.
Normal sideroblasts have one to a few scattered fine granules rather than coarse granules forming a perinuclear collar.
